lead: nothing you have ever been paid to do was new when it reached you. the fastest thing in you is built for a first minute, and your whole working life has been spent on second ones.
sun: the work is retrieval. a product shelved four years ago, an account that walked, a case somebody else closed and signed — these come to you because you are the one in the building who does not accept that a thing is over, and you are usually right. nothing in your record started as yours. every job on your desk was set down by somebody else, and most of them come up.
moon: speed is the wrong instrument for a second visit. you are inside the thing before anyone has asked you to be, at the pace of a first response, and a first response does not stop to read why it failed the last time. so you re-enter at full commitment, before the history is yours, and the second attempt goes down the same way the first did, faster.
pull: you are sent in only where there was a first time, and you arrive as though there had not been one. the speed and the work have never once agreed.
tension: the beginnings go to other people. twelve years of turnarounds and not one thing has been handed to you at the point where nobody had touched it yet — and the reason sits on your own record, where every entry is a rescue. the word on your appraisal is dependable, which is praise for what you do with a second attempt and describes nothing you would do with a first.
cost: a client who walked out and meant it takes your call, and the draft everyone gave up on comes back off your desk alive — rare, billable, and people who have watched it stop arguing. what does not exist anywhere in your working life is a thing you started. the fastest instinct you own has only ever been spent on re-entry.

lead: you go back every year, and every year the thing you have been carrying since you were fifteen stays in. the door was never shut, so there has never been an evening it could be set down on.
sun: leaving that house settled nothing, and was not meant to. you went at nineteen and you have been back for every birthday since, nothing withheld at the door — and the family reads that correctly, as love, which it is. what they have no way to read is the other half: no one there has ever been marked as somebody you are through with, so no part of you has left the table.
moon: a term ends on a day its carrier picks, and every day you might have picked turns out to be one you are about to be welcomed back on. so it stays in, exact and unspent, because saying it would cost the next visit its whole character — and a next visit is always booked. the timing is entirely yours and all of it has gone on deferral.
pull: every good evening at that table is another year it stays in. the welcome is real, and it has been the reason for the silence since before anyone could have handled hearing it.
tension: your sister stopped going and is discussed at length. you kept going and are not discussed at all, which the family experiences as peace and calls you the reason for it. she has said, once, that you let them off. nothing was let off — it is held, entire, and the holding is invisible by construction — and there is no way to say that to her that does not sound like the position of somebody who forgave.
cost: the family still assembles, and that is your doing: you were the one who went back first each time, so nothing between any of them has been allowed to harden. the same behaviour is what makes your own item undeliverable. a room reassembled by you every year has no seat in it for the thing you are carrying, and nobody in that room knows a term is running.

lead: there is money of yours in eleven different lives and no single figure for it anywhere, including in you. each amount went out on a different reasoning, from a different one of you, and not one has been called in.
sun: nothing you have put out reads as spent. an amount in somebody else's account is in transit rather than gone, which is why you have never chased one and never needed to feel generous about it — in your own understanding there is no giving in this, only a wait. four of them did come back, years late and unprompted, and those four are why the rest are still entered as live.
moon: no one in you holds the total. the loan to your cousin was made by a different party than the one that covered a stranger's rent, and the two have never compared notes, so the sum has no address in there. from outside it resolves into one pattern with a name, and the person who finally adds it up is showing you a number you have never seen.
pull: six people in you have each made one reasonable decision about money. the number they add up to has been read out to you once, by somebody else, and not one of you recognised it.
tension: used gets said, kindly, by people who have the list in front of them, and the list is accurate. what it cannot show is that no one drew it up on your side — eleven separate decisions, none consulted with the others, no policy anywhere. and the true account is not a defence: it means nobody in you ever decided to be generous, only a series of parties who each thought this one was fine.
cost: nobody has ever had to settle up to stay welcome here. a person sitting on three years of your money rings at midnight and gets what anyone gets, so completely that they stop noticing it is there. what no one has had from you is a gift. every amount went out live, entered by a party who has since gone quiet, and nothing here has any other condition.

lead: the body you are training for is one you had at twenty-three, and you have never once trained the one you have. it has not gone anywhere. every session since has been addressed to it.
sun: you come back to it at the load you left it at. eight years off and the first week back is set at the old numbers, because the numbers were never lost — they were put down. this works often enough to be dangerous: the movement is genuinely still in you, the shape returns inside a fortnight. what does not return on the same schedule is the tissue that used to carry it.
moon: what the body gets from you is not a report on itself. it gets a distance — measured back to a standard set in one year, by a body you were briefly in and have never stopped keeping in view. so there is no good day available, only a width. and the width was never going to close, which some part of you settled years ago without saying so.
pull: you have never grieved the body you had, because nothing in you accepts that it went. so you go on training for it, and the one doing the training is not invited.
tension: the physiotherapist wants one sentence from you and has stopped asking for it directly: that this is the shoulder now. you nod at everything else. so the rehab gets done as a route back rather than as terms, and it ends the same way each time, and by the fourth referral the notes have a word in them for a patient who will not hear it. everyone in that clinic thinks the word is denial.
cost: you walk into the same room at fifty with nothing to apologise for and no shame at the door, because a decade away from it never turned into a verdict about you — most of the reason you are still moving. the aim never changes, though. nine re-entries, all of them addressed to a body that is not coming back, and the same joint gives out every time.
